A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AutoSizer and AMS-SizingBench. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and matchable; appendix content is unchanged apart from numbering.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 report original circuit-simulation results, component ablations, and optimization-dynamics analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation experiments and ablations, revises the main results, and adds strategy-decision and search-space adaptation analyses.

M1.justification: The two-loop algorithm, agent roles, optimization pool, and Appendix B prompts remain unchanged. The actions and feedback thresholds highlighted in new Section 4.6 were already documented in v1; they do not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 24 SKY130 circuits with the same task requirements and difficulty groups. The newly discussed bandgap and switched-capacitor cases already belong to this benchmark.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains Genetic, BO, TuRBO, ADO-LLM, LEDRO, and EE-Sizer, and Table 3 retains the same ablation configurations. New assertions about fixed or random schedules do not include evaluated comparisons against those schedules.

E3.justification: Sections 4.5–4.6 add decision-trace logging and measurements of action frequency, FoM impact, and trigger timing by difficulty. The main simulator, LLM configuration, metrics, and stated budgets remain unchanged. Table 4's cycle counts of 110, 135, and 60 evaluations are not reconciled with the retained 100-per-loop and 300-total budget.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations and ring-oscillator analysis, v2 adds substantive diagnostics of whether strategy selection adapts and what drives search-space changes. Tables 4–5 provide a bandgap decision trace and circuit-specific behavior comparisons; Table 7 quantifies action frequencies, FoM changes, and timing across difficulties.

E5.justification: Both report three trials for the principal experiments and retain the existing uncertainty-reporting practice. Table 7 extends mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting already used in Figure 5(c); no new seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are specified. Changed uncertainty values belong to E6.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises FoM values and associated spreads for every method and difficulty. AutoSizer's Easy/Medium/Hard FoMs change from 33.4/33.2/60.2 to 4.4/36.3/4.5, and evaluations change from 57.8/130.9/128.9 to 38.9/42.2/63.6. Its Medium/Hard runtimes rise from 1049.8/1152.6 to 1359.9/1473.2 seconds, making LEDRO fastest in both groups. Success rates and Table 3 results remain unchanged. New diagnostic findings appear in Tables 4–7; the PDFs do not explain the headline numerical revisions.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same normalized FoM definition, feasibility conditions, and constrained optimization formulation. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs, and the new analyses introduce no substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: reflective two-loop sizing, the 24-circuit benchmark, and superior optimization performance. The added code link and supporting analyses do not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: Sections 4.5–4.6 newly interpret observed decisions as behaviors fixed/random schedules cannot replicate, evidence that the inner loop suffices for easy problems, and an emergent exploration-first policy. These extend the mechanism discussion, although corresponding controlled comparisons are absent. Existing qualifications and the impact statement remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract adds an explicit code-repository address, and Section 4.6 states that feedback signals are extracted programmatically without manual curation. Existing configurations, hyperparameters, simulation instructions, and prompts are retained; most summarized feedback rules were already in Appendix B.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds GenCellAgent and removes the OpenDevin citation. AnalogXpert's attribution is corrected, and several references receive publication updates. The substantive positioning against earlier circuit-sizing approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds two analysis subsections, a conflict-of-interest disclosure, and acknowledgments, updates publication front matter, and corrects 'trails' to 'trials.' The existing narrative, section sequence, and appendix prose are largely preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds a substantial diagnostic display block: Tables 4–7 present decision traces, behavior explanations, feedback signals, and action-frequency/impact/timing results. Table 1 and Figure 2 are relocated, and Figure 5 receives limited line and legend styling changes without changed plotted results. The existing appendix tables are renumbered from 4–5 to 8–9.

improvement.justification: The new diagnostics and explicit code location improve inspectability. However, Table 2's extensive numerical revisions are unexplained, Table 4's evaluation counts conflict with the retained budget description, and the new fixed/random-schedule claims lack controlled comparisons. These benefits and reporting concerns prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
